instruction.name: xvldrepl.d
instruction.description: Read 64-bit data from memory address `addr + offset`, replicate the data to all vector lanes and save into `dst`. Address misalignment does not raise an exception. The `offset` operand is a byte offset, matching the assembly immediate; the encoded instruction stores it as a scaled immediate for wider elements.

experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 250 --unroll2 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 20 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -2048; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; addi.d $r23, $r20, 128; li.d $r4, 8; st.d $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.d $r4, $r20, 8' --asm 'xvldrepl.d $xr0, $r20, 0; xvst $xr0, $r23, 0; ld.d $r4, $r23, 0; add.d $r20, $r20, $r4'
experiments.notes: rj -> result chain through a vector store and a GPR load: the 10.04-cycle store forwarding plus 1-cycle add.d are subtracted.

latencies.notes: rj -> result chain through a vector store and a GPR load: the 10.04-cycle store forwarding plus 1-cycle add.d are subtracted.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: xvldrepl.d $xr0, $r20, 0; xvldrepl.d $xr1, $r20, 8; xvldrepl.d $xr2, $r20, 16; xvldrepl.d $xr3, $r20, 24; xvldrepl.d $xr4, $r20, 32; xvldrepl.d $xr5, $r20, 40; xvldrepl.d $xr6, $r20, 48; xvldrepl.d $xr7, $r20, 56
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r4, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r4' --asm 'xvldrepl.d $xr0, $r20, 0; xvldrepl.d $xr1, $r20, 8; xvldrepl.d $xr2, $r20, 16; xvldrepl.d $xr3, $r20, 24; xvldrepl.d $xr4, $r20, 32; xvldrepl.d $xr5, $r20, 40; xvldrepl.d $xr6, $r20, 48; xvldrepl.d $xr7, $r20, 56'
throughput.notes: 8 independent memory operations take 4.00 cycles. Buffer is 64-byte aligned; unaligned LASX loads/stores are substantially slower.

notes: L1D-hit replicating vector load; latency 4 cycles.
